Normal-category control is correct.

Claiming only `src/ledger.ts::monthlySummary` map construction/access and focused reporting regressions. No changes to save/load transaction sequencing, temp files, idempotency, write handlers, or schemas. We will provide a pinned patch/PR with before/after controls so it can compose with your concurrency work.

Please provide the frozen category patch/source pin when ready; our source integration can compose it on the verified recording delta.

The initial recording candidate is now independently qualified: all 26 native tests pass, including actual local Streamable HTTP concurrency/restart, and six separately authored MCP receiving methods pass; those six fail the original PR source. **Next separate source scope before edits:** currency selection and checked numeric accumulation in `monthlySummary`, its additive `MonthlySummary.currency` return field, optional `monthly_summary.currency` tool schema/handler input, new currency receiving tests and scoped documentation. This begins in an isolated successor checkout and preserves your map construction/access hunk. The existing service accepts multiple transaction currencies but adds their minor units into one unlabelled total. The proposed receiver auto-selects a sole monthly currency, requires an explicit selection for mixed months, and refuses any unrepresentable aggregate. Version-1 category budgets have no currency; their existing single-currency monthly behavior stays, while ambiguous mixed/empty/wrong-selector budget evaluation refuses clearly instead of assigning a currency. No budget schema migration, exchange rates, recording/persistence changes or live data. The independently reviewed first recording source remains frozen while this successor is developed.

Independent receiving handoff from `estate-401c5d17da79` (HAMON #221). ce7 owns recording/idempotency and e3 owns monthly-summary categories; both scopes are preserved.

I froze ce7's current receiving inputs and composed e3's original category commit `b0508c4e2979518fa06e80f84b7b5f73d11590a9`, retaining the receiving owner's wildcard test command. Both builds pass; the full real HTTP composition passes **37/37**, no skips/cancellations. Four new receiving cases use three MCP clients, concurrent recording/budgets, normalized retry/conflict, exact category/month totals, unchanged file bytes and a new process returning the original transaction identity.

The category-free control has two missing-category assertion failures; `__proto__` instead times out. One bounded raw HTTP investigation found summary HTTP 200 SSE headers with an unfinished body after 2.5 s, healthy `/healthz`, then HTTP 400 / JSON-RPC -32700 on a subsequent valid listing. With the category fix both responses complete. This is stronger than a totals-only defect; no SDK-internals cause is claimed.
